A multi-author blog needs more than a name in the byline. Blogkit keeps profiles in one file and builds everything else from it.

### The Profile File

```yaml
jordan-alder:                       # the slug: authors/jordan-alder.html
  name: Jordan Alder
  aliases: []                       # other spellings used in posts
  image: img/jordan-alder.svg       # square-ish photo, shown as a circle
  tagline: Teaches with code, themes and exercises
  bio: >-
    Jordan builds learning material: exercises with hints, readable themes
    and small examples that run.
  links:
    - {text: Website, href: "https://example.org/jordan"}
```

Posts keep a plain `author: "Jordan Alder"` in their front matter. A post belongs to the profile whose `name` or `aliases` match, so you can add profiles later without touching old posts.

### What You Get

- An **author page** (`authors/jordan-alder.html`) with the photo, bio, links and all of the author's posts.
- **Clickable bylines** on post pages and on the homepage cards.
- An **author card** at the end of every post with a link to "All N posts by ...".
- **Filters and pagination** on the author page: pick a category or a tag to narrow the list, then page through ten posts at a time. The state is kept in the address (`#cat=Blogkit&page=2`), so a filtered view can be shared.

### Adding an Author

1. Add an entry to `authors.yml` and put the photo in `img/`.
2. Run `quarto render`. Blogkit writes `authors/<slug>.qmd` for you (never edit that file by hand) and the page is built.
3. Use the exact `name` in the posts' `author:` field.

An author who is not in `authors.yml` simply has no link, so guest posts still work.

This sample site has two authors, so you can see both pages and the filters in action. For how the data file reaches the browser, read [Welcome to Blogkit](welcome-to-blogkit.qmd).
